naval.label: Two Chinese-built submarines received by the Navy (December 2016)
naval.text: The Bangladesh Navy received two China-made submarines in December 2016. They were commissioned as BNS Nabajatra and BNS Joyjatra. They are conventional diesel-electric boats, 76 metres long, equipped with torpedoes and mines.

naval.label: Pekua submarine base inaugurated (March 2023)
naval.text: The Pekua submarine base, near the Kutubdia channel in the Bay of Bengal, was inaugurated in March 2023. It is Bangladesh's first full submarine base. It cost about US$1.21 billion and can accommodate six submarines and eight warships. Before it was built, the submarines were housed at a Chattogram naval base.

arms.label: Rooppur unit 1 cleared to start controlled fission (8 October 2026)
arms.text: Fuel loading into Rooppur unit 1 began on 28 April 2026. On 8 October 2026 the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority cleared the unit to begin controlled fission, the step before first criticality. Grid power is expected months later. Unit 2 is planned for 2027.
arms.source: New Age (8 Oct 2026); Prothom Alo (28 Apr 2026)

arms.label: Army-owned defence industries in Gazipur, Narayanganj and Chattogram
arms.text: Bangladesh Ordnance Factories, founded in 1970 at Gazipur, makes arms and ammunition. The Bangladesh Machine Tools Factory and the Bangladesh Diesel Plant are also Army-owned. Khulna Shipyard, Chattogram Dry Dock and the Dockyard and Engineering Works in Narayanganj are military-owned or navy-managed.
arms.source: Wikipedia; New Age; Bangladesh Steel and Engineering Corporation

air.label: Air Force drone plant planned with China (November 2025)
air.text: The Business Standard reported in November 2025 that the Bangladesh Air Force is setting up a drone manufacturing plant in a joint venture with China, with technology transfer. The plant's site has not been published, so the dashboard does not plot it.

air.label: Air Force bases (Bashar, Kurmitola, Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Jessore)
air.text: The Air Force's bases include BAF Base Bashar (Tejgaon, Dhaka: transport and helicopters), BAF Base Bir Uttom A.K. Khandker (Kurmitola, Dhaka: fighters; formerly Bangabandhu and renamed on 9 March 2025), BAF Base Zahurul Haque (Chattogram), BAF Base Cox's Bazar and BAF Base Matiur Rahman (Jessore).

mss.label: Chittagong Hill Tracts conflict: second phase since October 2022
mss.text: The first phase ran from 1977 to the Chittagong Hill Tracts Peace Accord of 2 December 1997. A second phase began on 20 October 2022, and Wikipedia records it as ongoing. Clashes with the Kuki-Chin National Front and infighting between the UPDF and the JSS have been reported.

mss.label: Khagrachhari clashes and blockade (23-30 September 2025)
mss.text: Clashes, road blockades and strikes in Khagrachhari district followed the reported rape of an indigenous schoolgirl in mid-September 2025. Several reports describe communal violence between indigenous and Bengali settler communities.
mss.source: Wikipedia (2025 Khagrachhari clashes); The Daily Star

mss.label: UPDF youth leader reported killed in Rangamati (17 April 2026)
mss.text: A UPDF youth wing vice-president was reported killed in Rangamati Sadar on 17 April 2026. The UPDF blamed members of the Jana Samhati Samiti. Both groups deny maintaining an armed wing.

milops.label: Army divisions and cantonments (published list)
milops.text: The Army's infantry divisions are the 9th (Savar), 11th (Bogra), 19th (Ghatail), 24th (Chattogram), 33rd (Comilla), 55th (Jessore), 66th (Rangpur) and 10th (Ramu, formed 2015). The Army's published list gives the cantonment towns; the coordinates are approximate.
milops.source: Bangladesh Army cantonment list; Wikipedia (list of formations)

social.label: Rohingya population in Bangladesh (UNHCR reporting)
social.text: UNHCR reporting puts the Rohingya population in Bangladesh at about one million, most of them in the Cox's Bazar camps. Conditions and figures are reported and contested.

scs.label: Bangladesh-Myanmar maritime boundary settled by the ICJ (March 2012)
scs.text: The International Court of Justice drew the maritime boundary between Bangladesh and Myanmar in the Bay of Bengal in its March 2012 judgment.

wellbeing.label: World Happiness Report 2026: Bangladesh ranks above India
wellbeing.text: India ranked 116th in the 2026 World Happiness Report, behind Pakistan and Bangladesh. Bangladesh's exact rank was not verified in this build.
